Room map format: $80 ends; $81-$FF = (n & $7F) literal tiles follow; $00-$7F = the next tile repeated n times. Tile: bit 7 = colour $F8 for both cells, bits 0-6 = char; the char goes to the upper row and char|$80 to the row below. 40 tiles per double row from $8C78.

Room map RLE: $80 ends; $81-$FF = the next (b & $7F) bytes are cells; $01-$7F = the next byte is one cell repeated b times ($00 would repeat 256 times). Cell: bits 0-6 = tile, the top char gets the tile and the bottom char tile|$80; bit 7 = colour RAM $F8 for both chars, else the room colour from $09DC stays. 40 cells per double row from $8C78.

End of map: redraw_taken_lanterns (which also runs the room init handler), display on, sprite enable restored, then run_room_update runs the room frame handler once; its RTS returns to the caller of draw_room.

Scans the keyboard when no key is pending and no joystick or key line is active. key_scan_mode 0 decodes the full matrix, 1 only F1, S, SPACE and V. When the scanned code differs from key_code, it stores it in key_code (column*8+row, bit 7 = shift) and, for a pressed key, sets key_pending to 1: one event for each press.
Full matrix decode: finds the first pressed key from the column mask key_columns and stores column*8+row in key_scanned ($FF none). Skips both SHIFT keys ($0F, $34).
Tests the four game keys in game_key_matrix; stores the matching code from game_key_codes in key_scanned, or $6F when none matches.
Game keys: 4 pairs (CIA1 port A column select, port B value when pressed) for F1, S, SPACE, V.
Key codes of the 4 game keys: F1 $04, S $0D, SPACE $3C, V $1F.
Masks $FE,$FD,$FB,$F7,$EF,$DF,$BF,$7F: one line low, used for column select and row test.
Key code of row 0 of each column: column*8.

Raster IRQ at line $63 of the player-up screen ($0EA7): waits for line $6D/$6E, then changes $D022 seven times to draw colour bars over the text, sets charset $8000 multicolour, rearms itself at line $63 and decrements frame_countdown.
Delay loop of 10 DEX steps (about one raster line).

Raster IRQ at line $FD of the title and game-over screens: decrements frame_countdown, counts attract_countdown down, selects charset $8000 multicolour for the upper part, runs the music player $E006 and sets irq_split_bottom at line $82.
Raster IRQ at line $82 of the title and game-over screens: selects charset $8800 and 38 columns with X scroll 6 for the lower part, and sets irq_split_top at line $FD.

Called once per frame by the game raster IRQ $48C1 (line $FB). Runs the sound engine ($EB03/$EF73/$F073 with the room in X), advances random_ptr, sets charset_hi from room_d018, shows the left-handed markers, advances room_timer, the idle timer and screen saver, the frame and attract countdowns, reads the joysticks into actor_joy_dir/actor_joy_fire and returns a human Yamo to the computer after a long idle time. Holds two copy-protection checks.

Called once per frame by the game raster IRQ irq_frame_top (line $FD). Runs the sound engine ($EB03/$EF73/$F073 with the room in X), advances random_ptr, sets charset_hi from room_charset_d018, shows the left-handed markers, advances room_timer, the idle timer and screen saver, the frame and attract countdowns, reads the joysticks into actor_joy_dir/actor_joy_fire and returns a human Yamo to the computer after a long idle time. Holds two copy-protection checks.
marker $2C at $8C2A (player 1) / $8C4D (player 2) when the joystick is left-handed
while playing and not paused: room_timer_lo/room_timer count up until room_timer reaches $80
Every 256 frames idle_timer counts up; at $80 the game pauses itself (pause_state=$86) and saves the colours for the screen saver.
While the screen saver is on: raster_colours = (saved colours XOR colour_cycle_counter) AND $F7.
Copy protection: loops back for ever unless the CPU port DDR $00 reads $EF (left by the original loader)
Every frame, also in the game: frame_countdown - 1 down to 0, and attract_countdown/title_timeout_hi - 1 as one 16-bit value down to 0.

Saves the CIA1 data direction registers, sets both ports to input and reads the current player's port (player 1 port 1, player 2 port 2) into actor_joy_dir/actor_joy_fire for Bruce, and the other port for a human Yamo.
Copy protection: when $02 is not $32 fills memory downward with that value and never returns
Copy protection: when $02 is not $32, fills memory downward from page $02 with that value; the page count is the code byte $0539 ($D0)
any joystick input (or demo mode) clears idle_timer
With a human Yamo: after 7*256 frames with no direction and no fire on Yamo's port, switches Yamo back to the computer, sets room_timer to $20 and takes 5 falls from both players (9 -> 4).

Per main-loop pass: calls $2D7C, in demo mode takes Bruce's direction (low nibble) and fire (high nibble) from the demo stream at (demo_input_ptr), then for each active actor (2..0) runs actor_move_step and $2780. In room 19 Bruce's direction is overridden: up while room_timer < 2, else none.

Prints message A from message_ptrs at text line X ($1A67), column offset Y. Text is in screen codes +$20, ended by $A0. Writes double-height text: code AND $7F on the upper row, code OR $80 on the lower row; when text_single_height is nonzero the lower row goes to $DE00 (discarded).

Bruce has fallen: in demo mode restarts via $0584. Otherwise decrements falls_left; at -1 goes to game_over, else (with two players) changes player, shows the player-up screen and re-enters the room through $3217.
Two players: exchanges zero page $28-$43 (falls, room, lantern counters, game_cycle, score) with other_player_state, then the lantern record states and the extra-life thresholds.
Re-initialises the game screen and Bruce, then respawns him in current_room (after a swap, the room of the new player).

Game-over screen: clears text lines, installs irq_split_top, draws the two strings at $42CD/$42DF, the player name from $4A5D/$4A6D and the score in big digits, waits $FE frames, then either continues with the other player or waits $40 frames and goes to $0584.
Draws digit A (low nibble) as a 2x2 block of characters $B4+4*digit.. at ($04),Y/($06),Y and advances Y by one.
Multiplies mul_value ($43BC) by 8 into the 16-bit value mul_result_hi:mul_value ($43BB/$43BC).
Multiplies char_addr_lo by 8 into the 16-bit value char_addr_hi:char_addr_lo ($43BB/$43BC).
In demo mode: fire on port 1 or the F1 key waits for fire release, waits 6 frames and returns to the title ($050F).
Counts the debounce field (bits 1-2) of pause_state down to 0 and then sets last_key to $FF.
While the debounce field (bits 1-2) of pause_state is nonzero: replaces bits 0-2 with that field minus 1 (6, 5, 3, 1) and sets last_key to $FF.
While paused and the debounce is over: the fire button of the current player's joystick toggles the pause off (falls into toggle_pause).
Flips bit 7 of pause_state and sets the debounce. Pausing shows PAUSED; resuming erases it, restores the colours if the screen saver was on, clears idle_timer, prints TOP and continues at $31C2.
Shows the player label and the PAUSED message and sets idle_timer to $51 (screen saver after about 47*256 frames).
Clears text lines 2-12 (both rows). Nothing calls it.
Clears text lines 0-12 (40 bytes on each row) and clears text_single_height.
Sets ($04) to the upper row and ($08) to the lower row of text line X from the tables at $4338/$434C and $4360/$4374; with text_single_height nonzero ($08) is $DE00.
Writes 0 to 40 bytes at ($04) and ($08).
Blinks the 1UP/2UP label of the current player on the status line: player_label_timer counts down from $20; at 0 prints the blank message 0, at $10 message current_player+1.
Blinks the 1UP/2UP label of the current player on the status line: player_tag_blink_timer counts passes down from $20; at 0 prints the blank message 0, at $10 message current_player+1.
Prints message 3 (TOP) on the status line at offset $38, single height.
Prints message 5 (FALLS) on text line 0 at offset $44.
Prints $E6, $E9, $5A and $5B as hex on the status line. No code reaches it (the RTS at $1AD0 comes first).
Converts falls_left to two BCD digits (bcd_tens/bcd_ones) and prints them on the status line at offset $4A.
Prints A as two decimal digits (characters $10-$19) at $8C00+Y and $8C01+Y.
Scans the game keys: F1 returns to the title, S flips sound_toggle, SPACE toggles the pause, V shows or removes the version line (text at $4707) on the top screen row.
Prints A as two hex digits at $8C00+Y and $8C01+Y (characters $10-$19, letters after them).
Prints message 11 (PAUSED) on text line 1 at offset $0F, single height.
Prints message A at line X, offset Y through print_message, then clears text_single_height.
Prints message 12 (blanks) over the PAUSED message.

Main game loop, at most one pass every 3 frames: demo exit check, game keys and pause, player label blink, light flicker, enemy spawn timers, room handler, actor sprites, actor input and movement, then waits until frame_countdown is 0.

Main game loop; one pass takes 3 frames or more. Demo exit check; in a game the game keys and the pause (a paused pass ends here); energy masks of actors 1/2, player label blink, light flicker, enemy timers and spawns, frame_parity, room handler, background collision and touches, protection key 2, sprite collisions, score and high score, actor input and movement, object sprites, knock-outs; then waits until frame_countdown is 0.
protection_key2 = $CF7A XOR $CF9A
Converts actor X's position to character cell coordinates: actor_char_x = (actor_x-12)/4, actor_char_y = (actor_y-12)/16 (actor_y+4 in room 13).

One movement step of actor X: waits for actor_anim_delay, records the moves of the last step, then chooses the next action from actor_joy_dir/actor_joy_fire, the terrain flags actor_flags_b6 and the current action, and moves the actor (up to 8 sub-steps).
Takes back the moves recorded for actor X (up, down, left and right counters at $4F63-$4F6E) and restores the previous move history; then sets action $18 with actor_action_timer $40.
Sets $B0,X to 2, moves actor X down two steps and sets action $0E.
Sets $B0,X to 2, enters at the second jsr actor_move_down ($1DBC), so it moves actor X down one step, and sets action $0E.

On the floor (actor_contact bit 0 or 2): actor_joy_dir picks the action. $0E up (climb or jump), $0D down, $0B left, $07 right, $09 down-left, $05 down-right, $0A up-left jump, $06 up-right jump, $0F none (fire = punch $11). Any other value gives idle. No floor contact: fall (actor_descend_two_steps).
With terrain bit 2 set moves actor X up; with bit 3 set makes it idle; otherwise starts action 5 with actor_action_timer $0F.
Moves actor X up one pixel (actor_y-1, top limit $2E) and sets action 1; blocked -> idle.
Moves actor X down one pixel (actor_y+1, limit $C7) and sets action 2; blocked -> idle.
Runs actor_left_or_fire_move twice.
When actor X is walking left (action 3, actor_anim_step < 4) and fire is pressed, starts action $0C with actor_action_timer $0C; otherwise moves left.
Moves actor X left one pixel (actor_x-1, limit $0D), faces left and sets action 3; blocked -> idle.
Runs actor_right_or_fire_move twice.
When actor X is walking right (action 4, actor_anim_step < 4) and fire is pressed, starts action $0D with actor_action_timer $0C; otherwise moves right.
Moves actor X right one pixel (actor_x+1, limit $A3), faces right and sets action 4; blocked -> idle.
Unless terrain bit 2 is set, starts action $11 for actor X with actor_action_timer 4.
Sets action 0 for actor X; counts $4FDB,X up when it was already idle.
Sets action A for actor X, loads actor_anim_delay from action_delay_table and clears actor_action_timer.
Sets action A for actor X with actor_action_timer $0F.
Sets action A for actor X with actor_action_timer $0C.
Sets action A for actor X with actor_action_timer 4.

Starts sound effect $80 (keeps A, X, Y) and runs two tamper checks: protection_key = 0 or protection_key2 = 0 slowly patch the key-reading code and finally write $9A (TXS) into random_byte or over tamper_trap, which crashes the game.
tamper check 1: protection_key must be nonzero
tamper check 2: protection_key2 must be nonzero
CLC; overwritten with $9A (TXS, X=4) by the tamper check
Copies of the CIA 1 data direction registers ($DC02/$DC03), saved at $1689 and restored at $1717 around the keyboard scan.
CIA1 DDR A saved during the IRQ joystick read.
CIA1 DDR B saved during the IRQ joystick read.
Anti-tamper value: $CF7A XOR $CF9A, written each main-loop pass at $1C13. When it is 0, $1FE5 changes code operands ($1C14/$1C17) and finally writes TXS ($9A) to $1FFE so that the game crashes.
$CF7A XOR $CF9A, computed each main-loop pass; checked by play_sound_80_checked.

Runs one step of the current action of object X (state $BF,X) with Y = remaining state timer $CE,X; moves the object and sets the next state and timer through continue_action_state, or ends the action. Entry code handles state 5 (jump straight up).
State $0C: flying kick to the left, rise for timer >= 10, then fly level, then drop until the floor (terrain bit 0).
State $0D: flying kick to the right, same arc as state $0C.
State 6: jump to the left, 2 px per step, rising for timer >= 10, falling below 7 until the floor.
Y = 3 here (actor_move_left stores its state number in Y), not the timer: never equal, so every falling step moves down 2
State 7: jump to the right, same arc as state 6.
Y = 4 here (actor_move_right stores its state number in Y), not the timer: never equal, so every falling step moves down 2
State $19: when the timer of object 0 reaches 1, jumps to $1818 (life lost); else the state continues.
State $17: climbing (terrain bit 2). Moves 2 px in the joystick direction every 5th step, plays the step sound, and rides along with the moving texture when $60 = 1 ($65 = direction).
State $10: enemy waits until its timer is 1, then appears facing the player.
Turns enemy X towards object 0, sets state $12 with timer $10 and plays sound $81.
State $11: punch; plays sound $85 at timer 8 and ends with recovery at timer 1.
never equal: actor_still_fire_move starts the punch with timer 4, so sound $85 is not played here
Ends the attack of object X: state 0 with timer 6, then sets the recovery timer from the progress check $10D0 (object 0: 3 or 12; enemies: 6, 3 or 1).
State $16: kick; plays sound $85 at timer 12, pushes the move counter forward and ends with recovery at timer 1.

State $16: the Ninja's strike, started only at $23C4. Contact bit 3 ends it. Plays sound $85 at timer 12, counts one move in the facing direction in actor_moved_right/actor_moved_left each step without moving, and ends with recovery at timer 1.
State $14: enemy AI. Uses the distance to object 0 ($2DDD -> $62/$63) to turn, walk towards it, start a punch, kick (state $16) or flying kick (state $0C/$0D).
Sets state $15 with a timer of the X distance to a point $0F beside object 0 (minimum 5).
Moves the enemy 2 px in its facing direction and keeps state $14.
State $15: enemy walks in its facing direction; at timer 1 it turns round and returns to state $14 with timer $80.
State $12: enemy appearing; only counts down the timer.
State $0F: hit; the object is pushed 2 px per step away in its facing direction; enemies recover at timer < 2.
State $13: knocked down; pushed 2 px per step (object 2 is thrown 8 px more at timer 10).

State $13: knocked down or knocked out. Each step: down 1 when contact bits 0 and 2 are clear, then 2 against the facing. At timer 10 the Ninja (actor 2) goes 8 more to the left when facing right, but 4 more to the right when facing left. An enemy with energy >= 0 recovers at timer 1.
State $18 entry check.

Last check of the chain. actor_move_step sends a running state $18 to action_blocked_step itself, so the states that get here have no handler (0-4, $0E, $1A, $1B): continue_action_state only counts their timer down.
State $18: while the object overlaps an obstacle (terrain bit 3) its last moves are undone from the move history ($1CD4); with an empty history it is put back into the room at $4BAE/$4BC2 via $2F8E.
Stores state A for object X, reloads the step delay $0106,X from $4A8C,state and sets the timer $CE,X to action_timer - 1.
Ends the action: state 0 (standing) through $1F92.

Y = sound id ($8x). Sets $D418 to $15 and starts the sound on the first free channel ($EB00/$EF70/$F070); when all are busy it replaces a channel whose sound has a lower priority (sound_priority_table by the low nibble of the id).

Y = sound id ($80 + effect). Sets $D418 to $15 and puts Y into the first free channel ($EB00/$EF70/$F070); when all are busy it replaces the first channel whose priority is lower or equal (sound_priority_table by the low nibble of the id); otherwise the request is dropped.
Clears the three sound channel ids and writes 0 to SID registers $D400-$D420.
Priority of each sound effect, indexed by the low nibble of the sound id.
Priority of the sound that plays on each of the three channels.

For each active object (2..0) copies its current frames ($4F4E,X and, except object 2, $4F51,X) into its sprite blocks of the buffer selected by $277D, keeps the width flags and colours in $D4-$DF, then clears sprite_frame_shown so the IRQ shows them.

For each active actor (2..0): copies frame actor_frame_a ($4F4E,X) and, for actors 0 and 1, frame actor_frame_a+1 into the actor's sprite blocks of the buffer selected by sprite_buffer_select; keeps the width flags and colours in $D4-$DF; then clears sprite_frame_shown so the IRQ shows them.

Called from the IRQ. Once per new drawing (sprite_frame_shown = 0): sets X (2 px units, X-MSB in $D010), Y (+$1D) and colour of the sprites of each active object, then points $8FF8-$8FFC at the drawn buffer and flips sprite_buffer_select.
wide body sprite and facing left: X - 8 (16 pixels)
overlay of relative frame 5, $19, $3F or $43: X - 8 (16 pixels)
Sets sprite pointers 0-4 to blocks 6-10 or 11-15 and flips sprite_buffer_select.

Copies a frame to the sprite block at ($0E), from row end offset Y backwards. Z clear = 16-px frame (2 bytes per row), Z set = 8-px frame (1 byte per row, column 0). Then clears the rest of the 63-byte block.
Source address of the 8-px frame copy, patched by setup_frame_source.

Y = bytes written (sprite_bytes_left EOR $3F); writes 0 from offset Y to offset 63. A narrow frame with height 21 (frame 129) writes 64 bytes first: sprite_bytes_left is then $FF and one 0 goes to offset $C0 of the block.
Source addresses of the 16-px frame copy, patched by setup_frame_source.
BRK byte after copy_wide_row: the loop always leaves by the BMI at $26F6, so nothing executes it.
A = hardware sprite number. Sets ($0E) to the data block of that sprite in the buffer selected by sprite_buffer_select.

X = frame number, $51 = object. Patches the copy source with the frame data address ($59BD/$5A8F), stores the frame height ($5B61) in $E0,obj, returns Y = height, A = colour ($5C33, or $F0 for object 2) and X = width flag ($5CBF).
also the exit of select_object_pose when the pose of this pass is already set
Addresses of the sprite blocks of sprites 0-4: buffer 0 $8180-$8280, buffer 1 $82C0-$83C0.
Sprite pointer values for sprites 0-4: buffer 0 = 6-10, buffer 1 = 11-15.
Hardware sprite of each object: 0, 2, 4.
Second hardware sprite of each object: 1, 3, none ($FF).
Bit of sprites 0-4 for $D010.
Inverted bit of sprites 0-4 for $D010.
0 or 1: sprite block buffer that is drawn next and shown by the IRQ.
0 = new sprite images are drawn and wait for the IRQ; set by update_sprite_registers.
$3F minus the bytes that copy_frame_to_sprite has written to the block; the clear loop runs until it is negative, so 64 bytes are written in all.

Chooses the animation pose of object X from its state $BF,X, timer $CE,X, facing $A4,X and terrain flags, and sets it with set_object_pose. Does nothing when obj_pose_done is set; saves the old pose in $4F54,X.
Y = pose. Stores pose and pose + 1 (overlay) in $4F48,X/$4F4B,X and the frame numbers pose + frame base of the character type ($59A5 by $95,X bits 7-6) in $4F4E,X/$4F51,X.

Reads sprite-sprite collisions ($D01E) into partner bits $B3-$B5. For each colliding object X whose partner attacks (kick $16, punch $11, flying kick $0C/$0D, drop $0E) and is in reach, sets hit bits in $BC,X; then applies the hits.
Skips objects that are falling, knocked down or dying; reads the partner object from sprite_owner_object and tests its attack.
Skips victim X in states $0F, $13, $18, $19, $1A and $1B; reads the attacker actor from sprite_owner,Y ($FF = none) and tests its attack state.
Y = attacker, X = victim. Sets bit 0 (hit landed) in the attacker's $BC,Y and turns the victim to face the attacker.

Per object: bit 0 = attacker recovery; bit 1 = kick hit (energy -2, state $0F); bit 2 = punch (-3, state $0F); bit 3 = flying kick (-7, state $13); bit 4 = dropped on (-5, state $1B). Bit 7 = hit by object 0, adds score ($3175). Energy below 0 = knocked out (state $13).
overwritten: the code falls through to the timer choice of actor 0 at $2B83
Energy below 0: knock-out score for hits by object 0 (more for object 1), state $13 with timer 12.
back to the bit-4 test: with bit 4 set the knock-out repeats until actor_energy wraps to a positive value
Y = attacker, X = victim. A = X distance of the victim in front of the attacker (sign by the attacker's facing), compared with the reach $61: C set when A >= reach.

Counts the scroll timer $60 down. When it ends: reloads it from scroll_speed_table ($4321 index; the index steps when scroll_moves runs out and the direction $65 flips when it wraps), moves the scroll offset $64 (0-7) and redraws three animated characters from 8-byte patterns at $42F1 (rooms 0-9) or $4309 (rooms 10-19).
Pause mode (scroll_timer bit 7, speed index 0 = $84): counts the low bits down without moving the texture.
Pause period over: reload the timer and count scroll_moves; when it runs out go to the next speed index.
17 moves done: anim_speed_index - 1; below 0 it wraps to 7 and scroll_direction flips.
Direction 0 (up): scroll_offset + 1 (7 -> 0); direction 1 (down): scroll_offset - 1 (0 -> 7).
Each frame: for every active actor whose energy (actor_energy) went negative, except while state $13/$19 still has a running timer: Bruce -> JMP $1818 (lose a fall), enemy -> remove_actor.
Bruce out of energy: lose a fall

For each live computer-controlled enemy (type bit 7 only when $42CA=0, type bit 6 always) that is idle (state 0, timer 0) with background-contact bit 0 or 2 set: starts state $14 with timer $14; if its previous state was $0C/$0D it instead resets it to idle with a recovery timer ($18, or 1/3 by random and game cycle).
For actor X: delta_y_to_bruce/delta_x_to_bruce = |actor - Bruce| on Y/X, clamped to $30, bit 7 set when Bruce is below/right of the actor.
Sets actor X to state 0 with timer 0 and action delay 0.
Sets actor_facing,X to 1 (right) when Bruce is to the right of the actor (delta_x_to_bruce bit 7), else 0.
Plays sound effect $86 through $2509; keeps A, X and Y.

Each frame: clears $0100, then for every active actor not dying (state $19): ends state $17, computes its cell position ($1C39) and checks the three cells at its row and the three cells one row lower with handle_touched_char.
Points ($04) at cell row actor_cell_row,X ($1A67) and passes the three chars at columns actor_cell_col..+2 (bit 7 cleared) to handle_touched_char. X = actor index in current_actor.

Dispatches on background char A touched by actor current_actor: $02-$05 exits, $62 sets state $17, $2D/$2E bonus fall (room 16), and when contact bit 1 is set: lantern chars $13/$14/$31 (Bruce only), deadly chars $0F/$40/$54-$5A (not $57)/$64/$71-$7C (and $66 from room 10), floor trap char $60.
$05 exit D
$02 exit A
$03 exit B
$04 exit C
needs contact bit 1
Chars $2D/$2E: the bonus-fall object, only in room 16; tested before the contact-bit check.
Lantern char: only Bruce collects it. Restores the background char from the room lantern list into both cell halves, adds 125 points and plays sound $8E.
125 points per lantern
Exit through char $02 when check_exit_direction allows it: destination exit_a_dest_room, entry exit_a_entry_x/y; an entry x of 0 falls through to the next exit table.
Exit through char $02 when check_exit_direction allows it: destination exit2_room, entry exit2_x/exit2_y. An entry x of 0 falls through to group 3.
Exit through char $03 when allowed: destination exit_b_dest_room, entry exit_b_entry_x/y.
Exit through char $03 when allowed: destination exit3_room, entry exit3_x/exit3_y. An entry x of 0 falls through to group 4.
Exit through char $04 when allowed: destination exit_c_dest_room, entry exit_c_entry_x/y.
Exit through char $04 when allowed: destination exit4_room, entry exit4_x/exit4_y. An entry x of 0 falls through to group 5.
Exit through char $05 when allowed: destination exit_d_dest_room, entry exit_d_entry_x/y.
Exit through char $05 when allowed: destination exit5_room, entry exit5_x/exit5_y (no fall-through).

A = entry x, Y = entry y, $4E = destination room, current_actor = actor. An enemy is removed (it left the room). For Bruce: sets his position and current_room, stores each active enemy's energy and Bruce's entry point in enemy_saved_energy/enemy_entry_x/y (they follow later), removes the enemies, resets the stack, draws the room ($09BC) and restarts the main loop at $1BC2.

A = entry x, Y = entry y, $4E = destination room, current_actor = actor. An enemy is removed (it left the room) and the char checks go on with the next actor. Bruce: sets actor_x/actor_y and current_room, saves each active enemy's energy and Bruce's entry point in enemy_saved_energy/enemy_entry_x/enemy_entry_y (0 for an inactive enemy), removes both enemies, SEI, reloads the spawn timers, resets the stack to $FF, draws the room, draws the actor sprites, CLI and restarts main_loop. Also entered from respawn_in_room and action_blocked_step.
drop return of handle_touched_char
new current room
For X = 2 (Ninja) and 1 (Yamo): an active enemy stores its energy and Bruce's new position (enemy_saved_energy, enemy_entry_x/y); an inactive one gets entry 0. Each is then removed.

Room 16 bonus object (chars $2D/$2E): when Bruce touches it with y >= $A0, uses one of the current player's bonus_falls_left, adds one fall, updates the falls display, plays sound $8E and erases the object.
one bonus use less for this player
extra fall
Draws tile string $56 (two blanks) at cell rows 10 and 11, column $24: removes the room 16 bonus-fall object.

Deactivates actor X: clears bit 0 of actor_flags, disables its one or two sprites in $D015, frees its extra objects ($EC/$EF via $0E21), clears its sprite data ($1131 for actor 1, $1145 otherwise) and continues at $0D42.
Deadly char touched (not in room 18): plays sound $8C; Bruce enters dying state $19 ($407D), an enemy is removed.
Floor trap char $60: if its colour RAM cell is not already 5, takes a free slot of trap_timer/trap_col/trap_row (cell minus 1) and sets the cell colour to $FD so the trap fires once.
